statements.text: As the power of technologies like Artificial Intelligence increases, lawmakers must be equipped with the knowledge needed to protect the American people.
statements.venue: Press release on bill to modernize technology knowledge in Congress

statements.text: AI is advancing so fast that it’s outpaced our regulations and guardrails. Moving fast and breaking things can’t include breaking public trust and human creativity. There must be oversight and regulation to protect consumers, creators, privacy, and our democracy.

With the recent explosion of large language models, language equity is an increasingly important issue that developers and auditors of AI must assess prior to making a model available for commercial or consumer use.
statements.venue: Letter to NTIA Administrator on AI guardrails

statements.text:
Election disinformation played a prominent role in the 2020 election cycle.
 
As Congress seeks to regulate AI, the FEC also has an obligation to combat this kind of disinformation. I sent a letter to the FEC this week to bring more attention to this urgent matter.
.@abc7breaking reports on my bill to hold spam callers like this accountable and protect from other AI threats. https://t.co/c7pqGlxy7R

You’ve seen the ways AI can mislead — that's why safeguards are needed as AI capabilities advance.

I sent a letter, alongside @SenAmyKlobuchar and @RepAdamSchiff, urging the @FEC to regulate the use of AI deep fakes in elections.
https://t.co/jqlxsE0NTY

Now, my question to you stems from, if people even know they are interacting with an AI system, which is not a given, so under that premise, isn't it then necessary that any transparency and oversight requirements be specific to the sector or use case of the AI system?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'The Need for Transparency in Artificial Intelligence,' Senator Lujan questioning a witness.

statements.text: Now, Professor, under the thought of the explosion of generative AI, which we know has serious implications for the integrity of our information ecosystems; do you agree that Congress should require tech companies to label any AI- generated content with disclosures and metadata that includes information on how the content was created?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'The Need for Transparency in Artificial Intelligence', where Senator Lujan questions an expert witness on policy options for AI-generated content.

statements.text: Now, the same type of transparency and easy-to-understand documentation is also needed so that consumers know where they are interacting with AI, know how their information is going to be used, and know when content is generated by AI. [...] And I am working on legislation to require this type of transparency and disclosures and responsibilities.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled The Need for Transparency in Artificial Intelligence, where Senator Lujan questions panelists.

statements.text: And, Mr. Gregory, yes or no, do you believe technology companies invest enough resources into making sure AI systems work equally well in non-English languages?
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI transparency where Senator Lujan questions a witness about unequal AI performance across languages.

statements.text: 3. Keeping communication open between advocates, unions, tech community, and Congress will be the only way to develop AI in a safe and practical way for American families.

1. AI has the capacity to do great things. It also holds a lot of uncertainties and potential for public harm.

2. There is little to no public accountability for AI, and Congress must act to minimize harm and maximize public benefit.

Today, I attended the first AI Insight Forum on Capitol Hill with @BillGates, @AFLCIO, Mark Zuckerberg and more top civil society and tech leaders. As Chairman of Communications, Media, and Broadband subcommittee, here’s what I know:

Congress must empower our regulators and enforcement agencies to ensure that when an individual or company breaks the law, they are held to account. Part of the reason these scammers are so effective at tricking consumers and evading enforcement is that the technology is constantly evolving. [...] Automated robocalls and robots are using chat bots and generative artificial intelligence to impersonate a real life person, lulling the recipient into a false sense of security by mimicking voices and mannerisms.
statements.context: Senate hearing on protecting Americans from robocalls, where Senator Lujan chairs and addresses AI-enabled voice cloning scams before entering a constituent victim's written testimony into the record.

statements.text:
BIG AI week this week & it’s only Wednesday.

On Monday, @POTUS signed an EO on AI guardrails. The same day, I led my colleagues in introducing bipartisan legislation for @NIST and @ENERGY to use facilities at our National Labs to test & evaluate AI to protect you from AI risks.

AI is revolutionizing so many aspects of our health care system, educational institutions, and workplaces. But without guardrails, it can do more harm than good.

Responsible oversight is critical to safeguarding our communities, and consumer protections must be paramount.
AI has the power to do both, which points me to the realization that AI is only as good as its inputs.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI in healthcare, Senator Lujan questioning a witness about biased training data in medical AI tools.

statements.text: An algorithm for diagnosing skin cancer on dermatologic photos will botch the diagnosis if the patient is dark skinned and most of the training images come from fair skinned.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI in health care where Senator Lujan questions witnesses about algorithmic bias.

statements.text: How can companies like yours work with Congress and other government agencies to ensure that full diversity of American farmers and farm workers have a say in the development and deployment of AI agricultural technologies?
statements.context: Senate hearing on innovation in American agriculture and AI, where Senator Lujan questions a private-sector witness.

statements.text: I think that is just a reminder that the Committee not lose sight of the human component here [...] Dr. Earles, California has a large Spanish-speaking population, as does New Mexico. Are efforts being made to make AI-enabled agricultural technologies easy to use by non-English speakers?
statements.context: Senate Agriculture Committee hearing on leveraging AI and technology in American agriculture.

statements.text: Dr. Earles, in your testimony you discussed research into how farms and workers can utilize AI technologies to monitor livestock, help provide nutrients, predict climate, and control irrigation. Yes or no, is there a work force ready to fully develop and operate these technologies so that farms across the Nation can fully benefit?
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI and technology in American agriculture.

statements.text: Deep fakes are interfering with our democracy from both sides, especially in our electoral process. Congress MUST place safeguards on AI to eliminate this election interference.https://t.co/khsCEmSvDo

On Tuesday, I sent a letter urging @FCC to take up the Declaratory Ruling to protect Americans from exploitative AI-generated robocalls.
 
Thank you commissioners for heeding the call and voting unanimously to protect the public and rebuild consumer trust.
statements.quoted: BREAKING: AI-generated voices in robocalls can deceive voters. The FCC just made them illegal https://t.co/ixxnkl5uNn

statements.text: She said it best — AI poses many unknown questions and risks. But it also can inspire ingenuity and acceptance for those fighting unique battles. Thank you, Congresswoman, for letting us in on your journey with PSP.
statements.quoted:
Your ears aren’t deceiving you—AI has allowed me to make a new model of my voice like it was before my PSP.

I hope this helps show creative ways we can empower people facing the kinds of health and accessibility challenges I have and demonstrate our abilities don’t define us. https://t.co/ztXDjCgi63

statements.text: One year ago at a hearing before the Senate Aging Committee, Gary Schildhorn testified about a call that he received that appeared to be from his son Brett pleading for help from jail. [...] Older consumers are a clear target of phone scams, personalized phishing e-mails, and other deepfake tactics. [...] Mr. Brookman, what is the most important thing that policymakers must do to protect older consumers from being scammed through these AI enabled tactics?
statements.context: Senate hearing on protecting consumers from AI-enabled fraud and scams, with Senator Lujan questioning a witness.

statements.text: AI is going to get tutoring to every student [...]
statements.context: Remarks by Senator Lujan during the Senate confirmation hearing for Howard Lutnick, nominee for Secretary of Commerce.

statements.text:
As Co-Chair of the National Labs Caucus, I'm proud of the strategic partnership between @LosAlamosNatLab & Open AI. This partnership will help LANL continue to develop cutting-edge tech & advance our national security, driving innovation right here in NM.
 https://t.co/JNVsO48Bo5
Do you see a role for the national labs in using AI for national security risk assessment?
statements.context: Question posed during a Senate Commerce Committee confirmation hearing for the OSTP Director nominee.

statements.text: AI has reached every sector in our country and driven innovation, but we cannot ignore the vulnerabilities and risks that come with it. While these systems have the power to change lives, they can also fall short – providing inaccurate or biased data – and are at risk of malicious attacks or misuse by our adversaries.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing the TEST AI Act

statements.text: Yesterday I reintroduced a piece of legislation called the ``Test AI Act'', which has bipartisan support, which would simply improve the Federal Government's capacity to test and evaluate in this area as well.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation'.

statements.text:
In the @commercedems hearing on winning the AI race, each witness agreed that the United States must invest in fast and affordable internet.

Senate Republicans are doing the exact opposite. https://t.co/fSkBvHt2zi

While AI can change lives, it can also spread bias, misinformation, and be exploited. We must also protect children from its harms and safeguard New Mexican jobs. I introduced legislation to test and evaluate AI systems, and I support standards that safeguard innovation without blocking states from enforcing their own protections.
I am also concerned by the increase in news stories reporting inappropriate interactions between AI chatbots and kids.
statements.context: Senate hearing on technology's impact on youth, where Senator Lujan uses his time to criticize AI chatbot safety records and demand executive testimony.

statements.text: While Americans are worried about rising costs and another war, Donald Trump is online posting AI images of himself as Jesus and attacking the Pope. Absolutely unhinged. https://t.co/Gq0M7wH7ug
I had to make sure this wasn’t AI. Sure enough, a speaker at Trump’s circus says God wanted the ballroom. You are not their priority.

statements.text:
As President Trump hosts President Xi, I’m joining @ChrisVanHollen and our colleagues in calling for serious negotiations with China on clear, enforceable guardrails for the most powerful AI systems. The U.S. must lead the world in setting standards that keep Americans safe. 
https://t.co/DYOIQHjIdD

AI is accelerating faster than our existing legislative processes, committee structures, and technical capacity can consistently evaluate and respond. The recent news of increasing incidents makes it clear that this is no longer a theoretical concern.

statements.text: We have the responsibility to understand and safely guide these technologies that are reshaping our economy, innovation, and national security before events force us to only react.
